name: Sensor Fidelity Optimization
consequences: Adjusting sensor configurations directly impacts data resolution and participant comfort. Prioritizing contact-free mattress sensors reduces physical intrusion but may lower event detection accuracy, while thermal imaging cameras mitigate privacy concerns but could obscure subtle movement patterns critical for parasomnia analysis.
options: Implement contact-free mattress sensors with pressure-sensitive arrays to reduce false alarms
Deploy ambient microphones with noise-canceling filters to isolate parasomnia-related vocalizations
Replace infrared cameras with thermal imaging to minimize privacy concerns while maintaining movement tracking
review: Sensor trade-offs between privacy and resolution risk underestimating rare events; options neglect long-term sensor calibration needs.

name: Staffing Model Reconfiguration
consequences: Modifying shift structures affects real-time response capabilities and technician fatigue. Extending night shifts beyond 12 hours risks operational errors, while part-time hires may reduce institutional knowledge retention.
options: Adjust night shift rotations to 12-hour blocks with mandatory rest periods between shifts
Hire part-time technicians from local universities to reduce fixed labor costs
Implement a cross-training program for technicians to handle both monitoring and emergency response
review: Flexibility in staffing introduces risk of inconsistent event management; options omit protocols for shift handover continuity.

name: Participant Recruitment Strategy
consequences: Expanding referral networks increases enrollment volume but may dilute clinical specificity. Direct outreach to non-traditional channels could accelerate recruitment while introducing selection bias.
options: Utilize social media campaigns targeting sleep disorder support groups for direct outreach
Offer extended stay incentives for participants with zero events to improve retention
Collaborate with local community centers for public awareness events
review: Broader recruitment risks lower clinical precision; options fail to address socioeconomic barriers to participation.

name: Annotation Process Refinement
consequences: Changing annotation workflows affects inter-rater reliability and throughput. Reducing human scorer involvement accelerates processing but may compromise diagnostic nuance.
options: Introduce a tiered annotation protocol where ambiguous events undergo consensus review
Use a single rater with periodic calibration sessions against a reference dataset
Automate initial event tagging using waveform morphology analysis for preliminary triage
review: Reduced human oversight threatens scoring consistency; options omit strategies for handling edge-case annotations.

name: Suite Capacity Management
consequences: Accelerating expansion beyond 8 suites strains safety protocols and increases maintenance demands. Delayed expansion preserves control but limits enrollment potential.

Convert adjacent residential units into temporary suites during peak enrollment
review: Scalability constraints risk missing enrollment targets; options neglect infrastructure resilience during peak usage.

name: Data Sharing Framework

Limit data sharing to internal use only to avoid regulatory complexities
review: Transparency risks compliance penalties; options omit strategies for balancing stakeholder access with legal constraints.
